Load functions and packages

Load the packages and other functions that will be used during reorganisation.

source('HS_functions.R')

Load data

Load the raw data

Load the raw data exported from Excel to csv.

path_file = file.path("0Data",
                      c(
                        "V_uncalib.csv",#vertical dances (not yet calibrated0)
                        "H_calib.csv"#horizontal and dome calibrated dances 
                        )
)
if(any(!file.exists(path_file)))
{print(paste(path_file, '\nnot found'))}
hd = lapply(X = path_file,
            FUN = read.table,
                header = T, 
                sep  = ',')

Combine calibrated and uncalibrated data

Check that all column names match across files loaded.

nm_vert = names(hd[[1]])
nm_calib = names(hd[[2]])
if(any(!(nm_calib %in% nm_vert) |
       !(nm_vert %in% nm_calib))
   )
{
  message("horizontal columns not in vertical")
print(nm_calib[!(nm_calib %in% nm_vert)])
  message("vertical columns not in horizontal")
print(nm_vert[!(nm_vert %in% nm_calib)])
}else
{print("columns match in all CSVs")}
## [1] "columns match in all CSVs"

Bind the tables together one set of rows on top of the other

hd = do.call(what = rbind,
             args = hd)

Inspect data

Exported CSVs sometimes end up with empty rows at the end. Check that the last row contains data.

print(hd[dim(hd)[1],])

Rename variables

Rename some variables with shorter or easier to recognise names. Video names currently include the full path for the user that annotated them these can be simplified to just file name and folder (date recorded). There are two kinds of grouping factor, firstly the identity of the individual bee, simplified here to ID, and within each individual bee their individual dances, specified here as ID_d. The date is now in YYYYMMDD format, this will be reformatted later.

#from the list above, identify unused or renamed columns to remove
rm_lst = c(
  "recording_type", #not used currently
  "source_batch", #not used currently
  "dance_key", #not used currently
  "dance_id", #renamed
  "bee_id", # renamed
  "date", #renamed
  "time_dance", #renamed
  # [8,] "waggle_run"
  # [9,] "condition"
  "orientation_method", #not currently used
  # [11,] "csv_file"
  "video_name", #should be identifiable from video_file
  # [13,] "direction_u"
  # [14,] "direction_v"
  # [15,] "video_angle_deg"
  # [16,] "true_north_video_deg"
  # [17,] "waggle_true_bearing_deg"
  # [18,] "mean_magnetic_north_deg"
  # [19,] "true_north_calibration_deg"
  "compass_circular_sd_deg", #not currently used
  "calibration_n_annotations", #not currently used
  # [22,] "calibration_quality_flag"
  "reference_compass_file", #not currently used
  "assigned_calibration_file", #not currently used
  "calibration_id", #not currently used
  "calibration_file", #not currently used
  "reference_landmark_file", #not currently used
  "landmark_dance_file", #not currently used
  "landmark_calibration_deg", #not currently used
  "landmark_calibration_circular_sd_deg", #not currently used
  "north_relative_to_landmark_deg", #not currently used
  "landmark_dance_video_deg", #not currently used
  "landmark_dance_circular_sd_deg", #not currently used
  # [34,] "start_x"
  # [35,] "start_y"
  "start_xy", #same as start_x, start_y
  "start_frame", #not currently used
  "notes"
  # [39,] "calibration_R"
  # [40,] "declination_deg"
)

#rename and remove unused or renamed
hd = within(hd, {
  ID = paste0(bee_id) # individual identifier
  ID_d = paste0(dance_id, "_", time_dance, "_", date) # dance identifier
  time = time_dance
  day = date # this will need to be converted to POSIX format

  video_file = file.path(
    basename(dirname(video_name)), #just the folder
    basename(video_name)
  ) # and file name
  #clean up information that has been doubled or will not be used
  rm(list = rm_lst)
})
#confirm resulting columns
names(hd)

##  [3] "csv_file"                   "direction_u"               
##  [5] "direction_v"                "video_angle_deg"           
##  [7] "true_north_video_deg"       "waggle_true_bearing_deg"   
##  [9] "mean_magnetic_north_deg"    "true_north_calibration_deg"
## [11] "calibration_quality_flag"   "start_x"                   
## [13] "start_y"                    "calibration_R"             
## [15] "declination_deg"            "video_file"                
## [17] "day"                        "time"                      
## [19] "ID_d"                       "ID"

Identify factor levels

Some of the character variables could be treated as factors. Inspect the different labels to each to check these are informative.

Click to expand full list 
nm_fact = c(
  # [1,] "waggle_run"
  "condition",
  # "csv_file", #easier to handle file paths as characters
  # [4,] "direction_u"
  # [5,] "direction_v"
  # [6,] "video_angle_deg"
  # [7,] "true_north_video_deg"
  # [8,] "waggle_true_bearing_deg"
  # [9,] "mean_magnetic_north_deg"
  # [10,] "true_north_calibration_deg"
  "calibration_quality_flag",
  # [12,] "start_x"
  # [13,] "start_y"
  # [14,] "calibration_R"
  # [15,] "declination_deg"
  # "video_file", #easier to handle file paths as characters
  # [17,] "day"
  # [18,] "time"
  "ID_d",
  "ID"
)
  
sapply(X = hd[, nm_fact],
       unique
     )

Add sun location

We can now use the time and date for each dance, combined with the location of the hive and feeder, to work out the relative positions of the hive, sun and feeder. This tells us what direction each dance should indicate for the feeder, as well as any potential effects of sun elevation on accuracy or skylight quality.

Set up times

First we need to combine dates in YYYYMMDD with times in HH:MM:SS to produce a POSIX/C99 “calendar time” for each. This is then converted to UTC for sun location estimation.

hd = within(hd,
            {
              time_code = mapply(FUN = paste, 
                                 day,
                                 time)#time in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS
              sast_time =  as.POSIXct(time_code, 
                                      tz = "Africa/Johannesburg", 
                                      format = "%Y%m%d %H:%M:%OS")#South African Standard time
              utc_time =  as.POSIXct(sast_time, tz = "UTC")#UTC time
              rm("time_code")#now duplicated
            }
)
with(hd, summary(utc_time))

In all cases time or date were available and could be converted, so it will be possible to calculate the sun’s azimuth for all of these.

Adjust for laptop clock (check this)

Videos recorded on the laptop have time stamps in CET not SAST. This means that they are one hour behind, since South African Summer time is UCT + 2, while Central European Winter is UTC + 1. Before calculating sun position, we should check that all times have been adjusted by adding one hour (60 minutes x 60 seconds). Below we estimate the correct time by extracting the time stamp from the video name and converting to SAST. This is then compared with the time generated from our notes, with a margin of error expected_diff. This is currently set to 5 minutes, which during the fastest rate of sun azimuth change of ≈2°/minute would result in a maximum sun azimuth error of 10°.

#upper limit of 5 minutes (x 60sec) between dance time and video saving
expected_diff = 5*60

extract_timestamp = function(string) {
  # Match a timestamp in the form: YYYY-MM-DD HH-MM-SS
  # Example: "2025-01-20 14-25-03"
  m = regexpr(
    pattern = "\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2} \\d{2}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}",
    text = as.character(string)
  )

  # Prepare output vector with NA values by default
  # This ensures every input gets a corresponding output element
  out = rep(NA_character_, length(string))

  # Identify which entries actually contain a matching timestamp
  ok = m > 0

  # Extract the matched substring only for entries with a valid match
  # substr() takes: start position, end position
  out[ok] = substr(
    string[ok],
    m[ok],
    m[ok] + attr(m, "match.length")[ok] - 1
  )

  # Return extracted timestamps, with NA for entries that did not match
  out
}

calc_expected_time =  function(cond,
                               ts,
                               sast)
  {
    switch(EXPR = cond, #by condition label
      vertical = sast, #these video names don't have a timestamp
      horizontal = sast,#these video names don't have a timestamp
      deg_10 = sast,#these video names don't have a timestamp
      antisolar = ts + 60 * 60, #these time stamps are in CET
      solar = ts + 60 * 60, #these time stamps are in CET
      zenith = ts + 60 * 60, #these time stamps are in CET
      sast # by default assume correct
    )
  }

#try to generate the expected time
hd = within(hd,
            {
             # Try to read the original video timestamp from video_file first, then csv_file, then ID_d
            video_timestamp_txt = extract_timestamp(video_file)
            video_timestamp_txt = ifelse(test = is.na(video_timestamp_txt),
                                         yes = extract_timestamp(csv_file),
                                         no = video_timestamp_txt
                                         )
            video_timestamp_txt = ifelse(test = is.na(video_timestamp_txt),
                                         yes = extract_timestamp(ID_d), #constructed in the same way as sast_time?
                                         no = video_timestamp_txt
                                         )
            video_timestamp = as.POSIXct(
                                        video_timestamp_txt,
                                        format = "%Y-%m-%d %H-%M-%S",
                                        tz = "Africa/Johannesburg"
                                        )
            #for all videos recorded on the laptop generate an estimated time, others use SAST time generated above
            expected_time = mapply(FUN = calc_expected_time,
                                   cond = condition, # experimental condition (determined laptop or camcorder)
                                   ts = video_timestamp, # time from video
                                   sast = sast_time, # time from notes
                                   SIMPLIFY = TRUE)
            #calculate difference between time calculated from notes and time from video
            oe_time_diff = as.numeric(sast_time - expected_time) # difference in seconds
            time_error = abs(oe_time_diff) > expected_diff # is difference larger than expected (logical)
            }
            
            )

#notify the user
if (any(hd$time_error)) {
  with(subset(hd, time_error),
       {
         message(paste('Time error found for:\n',
        unique(video_timestamp)
         ))
       }
  )
}else
  {
  print("All timestamps are close to observed time.")
  print("Differences in minutes (estimated time - notes)")
  with(subset(hd, condition %in% c("solar", "antisolar", "zenith")),
       {
         print(summary(oe_time_diff/60),
               digits = 2)}
       )
  #clean up new variables
  hd = within(hd,
              {
                rm(list = c('video_timestamp_txt',
                            'video_timestamp',
                            # 'expected_time' #keep in case this is needed later
                            'oe_time_diff',
                            'time_error'
                            )
                )
              }
              )
}

Estimate sun location

In order to determine the sun’s location (azimuth and elevation) we need to combine the time with the geographic location. GetSaz is a vectorised wrapper for oce::sunAngle, which corrects for refraction, but not the altitude from which the sun is viewed.

The current estimate of hive location is from a combination of Google Maps bookmarks and photograph metadata, cross-references with Google Earth satellite images.

# Hive position
# 25° 34' 18" S, 31° 10' 48" E
#-25.57167,      31.18000 

hive = r"(25° 34' 18" S, 31° 10' 48" E)" # N.B. this string contains literal " so needs wrapping in r"()"

# Define coordinates (lon, lat)
hive = Dms2decimal(hive) 

#add sun azimuth
hd = within(hd, 
            {
            sun_az = mapply(
                   FUN = GetSaz,
                   tm = utc_time,
                   lon = hive['longitude'],
                   lat = hive['latitude']
                   )
            }
            )

#add sun azimuth
hd = within(hd, 
            {
            sun_el = mapply(
                   FUN = GetSel,
                   tm = utc_time,
                   lon = hive['longitude'],
                   lat = hive['latitude']
                   )
            }
            )

print(with(hd, sapply(X = list(sun_az, sun_el),FUN =  summary)),

Add Feeder angle

To determine the expected dance directions, we need to know the azimuth angle between the sun and the feeder, for which we need the bearing from the hive to the feeder. As for the hive position, the current estimate of feeder position was determined
from a combination of Google Maps bookmarks and photograph metadata, cross-referenced with Google Earth satellite images.

geosphere::bearing requires coordinates in decimal, with longitude first and then latitude, so Dms2decimal converts from degrees, minutes and seconds to decimal and reorders the (latitude,longitude) vector.

# Hive position
# 25° 34' 18" S, 31° 10' 48" E
#-25.57167,      31.18000 

# Feeder position
# 25° 34' 14" S, 31° 10' 59" E
#-25.57056,      31.18306

hive = r"(25° 34' 18" S, 31° 10' 48" E)" # N.B. this string contains literal " so needs wrapping in r"()"

feeder = r"(25° 34' 14" S, 31° 10' 59" E)"

# Define coordinates (lon, lat)
hive = Dms2decimal(hive) 
feeder =  Dms2decimal(feeder)
#N.B. Dms2decimal converts from (latitude, longitude) to (longitude, latitude)
# to conform with geosphere::bearing

# Calculate bearing from hive to feeder
feeder_bearing = bearing(hive, feeder)
print(feeder_bearing, digits = 3)
## [1] 68.2
feeder_distance = distGeo(hive, feeder)
print(feeder_distance, digits = 3)
## [1] 331
#add feeder azimuth relative to sun position
hd = within(hd, 
            {
            feeder_az = Mod360.180(feeder_bearing - sun_az)
            }
            )

print(with(hd, summary(feeder_az)), digits = 3)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##   -30.0    22.6   161.6   109.0   172.6   179.9
print(with(hd, summary(abs(feeder_az))), digits = 3)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##   0.113  27.910 161.629 115.448 172.573 179.916

Based on geographic position alone, we can conclude that the feeder was at a bearing of 068° (approx. East-North-East) from the hive, ≈ 330m away. Given the hilly terrain, the ground distance flown may have been slightly further. After subtracting the sun’s azimuth, we see that the sun ranged between nearly 180° West of the feeder (presumably sunset) and precisely aligned with the feeder (presumably during the morning).

Format angles

Calculate angular error mismatch between u/v components and reported video angle. Identify and report any problematic dances with errors exceeding 1°, reporting their IDs, tracked directions, and source video files. Handles edge cases by setting direction and angle values to NA where the tracked direction is a zero vector (no angle tracked).

#check angle format

est_err = with(hd, {
    (atan2(y = direction_v, x = direction_u) + pi/2) - rad(video_angle_deg) 
  })
abs_est_err = mod_circular(abs(est_err))
#these can be out by as much as 1/(1000 000 000 000) of a degree
hist(x = abs(deg(abs_est_err)), 
     breaks = 1e2,
     xlim = c(0, 180),
     # xlim = c(min(abs(deg(abs_est_err))[abs(deg(abs_est_err))>0]), 180),
     xlab = 'absolute error in video angle',
     # log = 'x',
     main = paste0('maximum error: ', signif(max(abs(deg(abs_est_err))), 3), "°" )
      )

if(any(abs_est_err > 1))
{
  message("dances with error >1°:\n")
cbind(with(hd[abs_est_err > 1,],
     as.character(unique(ID_d))),
          unique(deg(abs_est_err[abs_est_err > 1])) )
message("tracked directions and video files:\n")
with(hd[abs_est_err > 1,],
           cbind(
     as.character(unique(ID_d)),
          unique(paste(direction_v, direction_u)), 
     unique(as.character(video_file))
     )
)
#these are zero length vectors
#set them to NA
hd = within(hd, 
            {
              direction_v[direction_v ==0 &
                          direction_u ==0
                          ] = NA
              direction_u[direction_v ==0 &
                          direction_u ==0
                          ] = NA
              video_angle_deg[direction_v ==0 &
                          direction_u ==0
                          ] = NA
            }
            )
}else
{print("no dances with error >1°")}

##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
##    0.16   38.84   60.65   98.06  108.04  359.85

Dance orientation measurements vary depending on the experimental condition. Some use compass-corrected bearings whilst others rely on video alignment. To enable consistent analysis across all conditions, we need to consolidate these angles into standard formats.

  1. Select the best angle measurement for each dance based on its experimental condition:

  • Use waggle_true_bearing_deg (compass-corrected) for most conditions (horizontal, deg10, antisolar, solar, zenith)

  • Use video_angle_deg (video-aligned) for vertical dances only

  1. Convert to multiple formats:
  • bearing: the selected raw angle in degrees [0°, 360°]
  • signed_angle: bearing in [-180, 180]°
  • angle: signed angle converted to radians \([-\pi, \pi]\)

  1. Remove the temporary video_angle_deg column

  2. Display summary statistics of all three angle representations

#assign angles to numeric

#video_angle_deg is the dance angle clockwise rel to vertical, except  error
hd = within(hd, 
            {
              # bearing = deg(atan2(y = direction_v, x = direction_u) + pi/2) %% 360
              bearing = mapply(FUN = switch,
                               EXPR = condition,
                               vertical =  video_angle_deg + sun_az, #aligned by default
                               horizontal = waggle_true_bearing_deg, #corrected with compass
                               deg10 = waggle_true_bearing_deg,
                               antisolar = waggle_true_bearing_deg, #now calibrated
                               solar = waggle_true_bearing_deg, #now calibrated
                               zenith = waggle_true_bearing_deg, #now calibrated
                               video_angle_deg + sun_az
                              )
              dance_sun_angle = Mod360.180(bearing - sun_az)# angle between dance and sun
              signed_angle = Mod360.180(bearing)  # bearing between -180 and 180
              angle = rad(signed_angle)# circular format is not needed for organising
                               
              rm('video_angle_deg')
            }
            )

sm_angles = with(hd, sapply(list(bearing, signed_angle, angle), FUN = summary))
colnames(sm_angles) = c("bearing", "signed_angle", "angle")
print("Final angular values")
## [1] "Final angular values"
print(
sm_angles,
digits = 2
)
##         bearing signed_angle angle
## Min.       0.16         -180 -3.14
## 1st Qu.   69.05           15  0.26
## Median   242.92           61  1.06
## Mean     244.14           40  0.69
## 3rd Qu.  427.61           88  1.53
## Max.     535.60          180  3.14

Calculate dance offset from feeder

To compare the dance angles against the true feeder direction, we calculate the angular offset between each dance and the expected feeder bearing, measured relative to sun position or the vertical .

  1. Calculate the angle between the dance bearing and the feeder bearing.

  2. Convert to absolute angle in degrees for easier interpretation.

  3. Print summary statistics of dance accuracy (absolute offset) for each experimental condition

#assign angles to numeric

hd = within(hd, 
            {
              feeder_angle = mod_circular(rad(dance_sun_angle - feeder_az))# angle between dance and expected dance
              abs_feeder_angle_deg = deg(abs(as.numeric(feeder_angle)))# absolute angle in numeric format
            }
            )
print("Absolute dance offset from true feeder bearing.")
## [1] "Absolute dance offset from true feeder bearing."
for(stim in unique(hd$condition))
{
  print(stim)
print(
  with(subset(hd, condition %in% stim), summary(abs_feeder_angle_deg)),
  digits = 2
)
}

On average, vertical dances are ≈20°–25° from the expected direction. Horizontal dances are less accurate, ≈30°–50° from the expected direction. For the other conditions divergences are much larger. For solar skylight in particular, there appear to be more dances opposite the feeder than towards it (half of dances >140° from feeder).

Plot example feeder angles

Plot individual examples from each condition relative to the correct feeder direction.

  1. Loop through each experimental day

  2. Identify the first dance for each condition

  3. Plot the angular offset to the expected feeder bearing, showing sun azimuth in yellow for reference.

for(example_day in unique(hd$day))

for(stim in unique(hd$condition))
{
example_lst[[stim]] = with(subset(subs_day, condition %in% stim),
                           unique(ID_d)[1])
}
#inspect
print(paste("First dance for each condition on", example_day))

                      ID_d %in% paste(unlist(example_lst))

As before, we notice that not all dances align well with the expected direction. This likely results from a combination of sun azimuth and elevation, as well as the part of the sky that is visible.

Write out reorganised data

In the final data frame, we can remove some of the variables used only to check data quality, since those checks have now been performed (or can be added) above.

# names(hd)

  # "waggle_run",
  # "condition",

  "direction_u",
  "direction_v",
  "true_north_video_deg",

  "true_north_calibration_deg",
  # "calibration_quality_flag",

Now that the data has been successfully reorganised, write out just the simplified data frame to CSV, in the same location as the original files.

# Write out table

write.table(x = hd,
            file = file.path(unique(dirname(path_file))[1], "hs_dance_reorg.csv"),
            sep = ',',
            row.names = FALSE
            )
